# Tiny Ledger

> An event-sourced banking ledger — accounts, deposits, withdrawals, balances — built as a Spring
> Modulith modular monolith in Java 25. It runs as a single JDK process with no infrastructure, or
> against Postgres, Redis, Kafka and Keycloak, from one codebase and one set of domain classes.

Written as a take-home exercise. The code was generated by AI under human design direction, and the
repository is documented so that claim can be checked rather than taken on trust.

Two things are worth knowing before reading anything else. **`docs/spec.md` is the contract** — where
it and the code disagree, that is a defect, and its *Open issues* section lists the divergences known
at the current version rather than leaving them to be discovered. **`docs/_archive/` is not
documentation** — it holds the agent execution plans that produced the code, kept for traceability;
where an archived plan and the spec disagree, the spec wins.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what it is, prerequisites, and a three-command quick start that reaches a
  working deposit with no infrastructure
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): the two run modes, the module boundaries, the domain
- [Documentation index](docs/INDEX.md): routing table for everything below, by the question being asked

## The contract

- [Specification](docs/spec.md): API shape, error catalogue (§6.5), security model (§6.4),
  idempotency (§6.3), run modes (§1), module boundaries (§3–§4), scenario catalogue (§9.3),
  non-goals (§13), documented assumptions (§15)
- [OpenAPI](docs/api/openapi.yaml): the request/response contract; server interfaces are generated
  from this file, not hand-written

## Decisions

- [ADR 0001 — How domain events reach Kafka](docs/adr/0001-kafka-delivery-path.md): outbox vs
  Modulith externalization, and the transaction boundary that makes it correct
- [ADR 0002 — Postgres as the event store, Kafka as the bus](docs/adr/0002-postgres-event-store.md):
  why the system of record is a database, reversing the author's own prior design
- [ADR 0003 — Test topology and CI parallelisation](docs/adr/0003-test-topology-and-ci-parallelisation.md):
  one Spring context per profile, and why CI splits by infrastructure need

## How it was built

- [Agentic workflow](docs/agentic-workflow.md): the pipeline, the skills used and their provenance,
  §5 where the agents were wrong, §6 decisions taken against agent advice, §7 the per-phase gate record
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what any coding agent reads before touching this repository — the enforced
  rules and the traps already paid for
- [Review artefacts](docs/_archive/reviews/): the council reports and assessments as written, so the
  review claims above can be checked against their sources

- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): what shipped, per branch
